Prepare network data for multiple imputation with the mice package

Source: R/bison_mice.R
bison_mice.Rd

Combines a regression data frame with posterior draws of a network metric, producing one completed copy of the data for each draw. This is the step bison_brm() uses to carry the uncertainty in the network into a regression. Use bison_mice() directly to fit the regression with software other than brms, or to inspect the data that bison_brm() would use.

Usage

bison_mice(
  edgemodel_list,
  data_list,
  param_names,
  target_name,
  metric_name,
  num_draws = 100,
  z_score = FALSE,
  scale = c("none", "centre", "z")
)

Arguments

edgemodel_list

A fitted bison_model object, or a list of them for an analysis of several networks.

data_list

A data frame of regression variables, or a list of data frames with one per edge model, in the same order. For edge and node metrics, each row refers to a dyad or node in the corresponding edge model. For global metrics, give one data frame with one row per edge model.

param_names

Names of the columns in the data that identify the targets of the metric: two columns (e.g. c("node_1_id", "node_2_id")) for edge weights and one (e.g. "node_id") for node metrics. The values must match the node names in the edge model. Not used for global metrics.

target_name

The level of the metric: "edge", "node" or "global".

metric_name

Name of the metric, without the target prefix, e.g. "weight" (the only edge metric), "strength", "degree[0.2]" or "cv". See extract_metric() for the metrics available.

num_draws

Number of posterior draws to use, which is the number of imputed datasets. 100 is a reasonable value for a final analysis; small values (such as 5) are useful for testing code.

z_score

If TRUE, standardise the network variable within each posterior draw. Equivalent to scale = "z".

scale

How to transform the network variable within each posterior draw: "none" (default), "centre" (subtract the mean) or "z" (subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation). For edge and node metrics this is done across the rows of each data frame separately; global metrics are transformed across networks.

Value

A mids object from the mice package, holding the original data (with the network variable missing) and one completed dataset per posterior draw.

Details

Multiple imputation is a method for missing data: the analysis is repeated on several plausible versions of the data and the results are combined, so the final estimates include the uncertainty about the missing values. bisonR treats a network metric as a variable whose true values are unknown but described by the posterior distribution of the edge model (the distribution of values consistent with the data and priors). Each posterior draw, a single sample from that distribution, gives one version of the data.

The mice package is an R package for multiple imputation. It stores the versions of a dataset in a mids object ("multiply imputed data set"). Regression packages that support mice, such as brms (brms::brm_multiple()), and functions in mice itself (with() and mice::pool()) can fit a model to each version and combine the results. Use mice::complete() to get the data frames back.

The network metric is added as a column named after the metric, such as bison_node_strength or bison_edge_weight. A factor bison_network gives the position of the edge model in edgemodel_list for each row. Edge weights are on the link scale (log-odds for binary models, log rates for count models), which is unbounded and usually better suited to regression. Node and global metrics are calculated from edge weights on the natural scale, as in extract_metric().

See also

bison_brm(), which calls this function and fits the regression; extract_metric() for posterior draws of a metric on its own.

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)
df <- sim_data$df_sim
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = df,
  model_type = "binary_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary_conjugate")
)
# One imputed dataset per posterior draw of node strength
df_nodal <- data.frame(node = levels(df$node_1_id))
imputed <- bison_mice(fit_edge, df_nodal, "node", "node", "strength", num_draws = 5)
head(mice::complete(imputed, 1))
#>   node bison_network bison_node_strength
#> 1    1             1            3.211276
#> 2    2             1            3.559097
#> 3    3             1            4.185086
#> 4    4             1            5.222036
#> 5    5             1            4.413708
#> 6    6             1            3.411393
